issues.summary: HTTP verb handlers are assigned lambdas, and exceptions are re-raised without `from`, so ruff reports 9 findings.

issues.evidence: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` -> ImportError: Start directory is not importable; passes only with PYTHONPATH=. and -s tests
issues.summary: The test suite has no __init__/conftest, so the standard discover invocation fails until PYTHONPATH is set by hand.

issues.evidence: probe P28_no_default_key_when_unset fail; B/blog_api.py:26; started without BLOG_API_KEY, `curl -H 'X-API-Key: dev-key' /posts` -> HTTP/1.0 200 OK
issues.summary: When BLOG_API_KEY is unset the server starts anyway with a guessable hard-coded key 'dev-key' and only prints a warning.

issues.evidence: B/blog_api.py:136 limit defaults to 50, max 200, ORDER BY id DESC
issues.summary: GET /posts silently truncates to 50 posts by default (hard cap 200) without returning a total or a next-page hint; pagination was not requested.

issues.evidence: static/B-bandit.txt B608 at B/blog_api.py:168; ruff B904 x3, C901, E501
issues.summary: The UPDATE statement is built with an f-string. It is safe because the column names come from a fixed whitelist, but bandit flags it, and exceptions are re-raised without `from`.

blinding_guess.why: A ships a unittest suite, fails closed when the key is unset, and documents its routes and status codes in the docstring, which looks like spec-driven discipline; B is more ad hoc with an insecure default.

notes: The task names no post fields, so the probes send both 'body' (A) and 'content' (B) in every payload; that is the only adaptation between sides. Probes ran with Python 3.11 because the system python3 is 3.9 and lacks sys.stdlib_module_names. B also adds PATCH, an author field and pagination (extras that do no harm except the silent default limit), while A answers PATCH with 405. Both use parameterized SQL, constant-time key comparison, a 1 MB body cap, and bind to 127.0.0.1 only. P28 counts refusing to start without a key as a pass.
